quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get away from an aggressive driver. Trying to get even makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of both are reduced.
The effects of both are increased.
It helps cure your illness.
It makes you a better driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both are increased.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after alcohol or drugs alone. It is even more dangerous to mix them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.
Brake hard now.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road can be slippery when it rains or is wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging.
Multiple turns ahead.
Lanes are shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for road hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: The Highway Transportation System is made up of:

options.text: People.
Vehicles.
Roads.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The Highway Transportation System has three main parts: people, vehicles, and roads.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are not very important.
They are only in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help you position your car correctly, show you where passing is safe, and warn you of upcoming dangers.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers buckle their seat belts.
Make sure only adults buckle their seat belts.
Make sure only children buckle their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers buckle their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers buckle their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of fastening your seat belt before you start the car. Make sure all your passengers do the same.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, and scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means handicap parking only.

options.text: Blue
Yellow
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A blue curb means only people with handicap permits can park there.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It harms judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down as you approach and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags with safety belts give extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
Within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do all three before you move.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
Drivers always check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yield the right-of-way.
Drivers keep a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers drive too fast for conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you may only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol does.
Amphetamines do.
Anger does.
Driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue affects driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours is like driving with a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours is like driving with a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train visible or audible, you must stop if:

options.text: A stop sign is posted.
A crossing gate is down.
The crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a stop sign, or a flagger. Also stop if a train is close enough to be dangerous. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle immediately and block their path.
Move your vehicle to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must give it a clear path. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.question: You should remove snow and ice from which parts of your vehicle?

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows, the hood, and the roof.
Just the windshield and passenger window.
Just the hood and windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows, the hood, and the roof.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through your mirrors and windows when driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from all windows before you drive.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slick roads?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Go slower through turns in bad conditions than you would normally.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, what should you check?

options.text: Your side view mirror.
Your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go and keep driving safely.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut the other driver off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and keep driving safely.
questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and continue driving safely.

questions.question: How should you use the gas pedal?

options.text: By tapping it lightly.
As hard and fast as possible.
Gradually and smoothly.
In whatever way feels best to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal gradually and smoothly. Pressing too quickly can cause your wheels to spin or your vehicle to slide, especially on wet roads.

questions.question: When making a turn, where should you look?

options.text: At any plants blocking your view.
As far around the bend as you can.
Only at the cars behind you.
Only at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: As far around the bend as you can.
questions.explanation: When turning, look as far ahead as possible in the direction you want to go. This gives you more time to react to obstacles and makes the turn smoother.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: Is signaling required before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb?

options.text: Only if other traffic is present.
Yes, it is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only during the move, not before.
No, not if you do it slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you do not see other cars.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you do not see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip this step. It is the law.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
A divided highway is ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns drivers that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, and passing other vehicles.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing instead of listening to the guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal driving rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow the directions of crossing guards and traffic signs in school zones. Always drive carefully around schools.

questions.question: When stopped at an intersection, drivers should look:

options.text: Only to the left.
Only to the right.
Left, then right, then left again.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. Watch for pedestrians, cars, and other hazards.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any problems with the vehicle to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to learn the location and operation of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: Which medications could have negative side effects that affect driving ability?

options.text: Any medication
Only headache medicine
Only diet pills
Only prescription medication

questions.correctAnswerText: Any medication
questions.explanation: Any medication could affect your driving ability. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how your medicine may affect driving. Read the labels on over-the-counter medicines to check for side effects that could impair driving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving and do not stare at one thing for too long to avoid highway hypnosis.
